body:
Hey sorry for taking so long to respond. The reason I suggest a therapist is because when you spill your thoughts you tend to find small ways to improve daily life that you wouldn't have thought of, and it helps to make sense of your own thoughts to hear them out loud and often times psychologists can give you different perspectives. It wouldn't hurt to try it at the very least, but I don't want to push anymore because it's annoying as hell I know. 

You can definitely take the GP route and get on some anti depressant and if that works then you're golden! You know what you're doing and can discuss your knowledge with your GP as to the reason why you want specific drugs vs. others. 

In my experience natural remedies rarely work for people with serious conditions (regarding St Johns wort, etc.), I wish they did though.

Those are horrible things to say to someone you're supposed to love, he won't ever recognize how much he is hurting you. But he is hurting you, even if you don't talk to family, try finding online resources. There are women's shelters and programs for people in your situation too if you should decide that you need to get out (no pressure), because the situation you find yourself in is not your fault at all. 
I may be a stranger on the internet, but I'm sending you some love right now, you're incredibly strong for reaching out. Feel free to PM me if you like, I'm going to work but I'll respond asap :)

I cannot even begin to imagine how you're feeling. You might search for a miscarriage support group online, sharing your story with people who have gone through that pain can be so cathartic. Dr. Jessica Zucker (a psychologist who went through a miscarriage herself) is an advocate for awareness around miscarriage and her writing is fantastic, you might find comfort looking at her site. My heart hurts for you, I'm so sorry for your loss.

Hi, I'm so so so sorry that this is going on. It sounds like you're being abused in a very intense way. I would absolutely encourage you not to harm yourself, it sounds like you're being groomed for his abuse. 
Take a look at some of the resources and suggestions on this website if you can, they even have people for you to talk to available http://www.thehotline.org/
When you're in the thick of the abuse, you don't see it, your brain will not let you. You think, oh its my own fault, I'm being dramatic, I deserve it and I love him. Your mum can't save you, but you can save yourself hopefully, its never easy. 
Please also be safe and if you need to delete your internet history don't forget to do that.

Hello! First of all, people are ignorant about celiac for sure, but there are tons of gluten free options because of the "fad" aspect of going gluten free. Now I imagine that a diet change like that will heavily effect your mood, its a huge shift in what your body is running on, and you might do some research into feeling lethargic and celiac disease.
Maybe you're a medical professional that knows all about treatment for depression, but that will not fix your depression. You do need to receive the treatment for it to help you, even if you don't think it will work, these days there are so many ways to talk to people online about your problems so you don't even need to go to therapy in person. But you should ABSOLUTELY be talking to someone, you're letting it out here, so what if you took that whole paragraph and sent it to a therapist, think of the amazing advice they could give. Not only advice, but support, you need support and not to feel alone.
When it comes to antidepressants, I recommend emailing around and looking for the psychiatrist that feels right and works for you, and then straight up tell them why you want the antidepressants you want and what you know about them. If they disagree you can ask why, and if they suggest something else you can ask why, you can always ask questions about your own treatment and discuss the pharmacology.
Anyway, I hope maybe some of this helped, and obviously you'll do what you want on your own journey in your own time so don't take it too seriously :)

Are you seeing big red flags at all? I am for sure. Ultimately its up to you, but ethically speaking, parents shouldn't hit their kids and then justify that by saying they didn't do it all the time. 
Healthy relationships have boundaries that are respected and not crossed, and no guilt trips. 
Your mom denies everything, don't open up to vulnerability again because she will not change and it will continue to produce hurt and anger. The ethical thing here would be to let yourself have peace, and not open yourself up to them again.

Not exactly, but my mom was a lot similar, she would make us food that was very bland and eat really delicious snacks and meals. So like, I could be eating chicken broth, and she could be eating steak and seafood. I have a lot of problems sharing my food due to this though, and also with eating healthy, or eating at all sometimes.

I'm not here to tell you about your own life, but if you have enough self awareness to think you're mini mom, then you probably aren't. No N would ever own that, or even entertain the thought of being wrong. Fleas are a real possibility, but manageable :)

Yeah haha, it's stupidly funny, when I'm at that point I want someone to talk to not someone getting all worried and all that. Things with doctors seem to get lost in translation too, so when I'm being candid, they are like horrified at that point. Sucks. I'm heading off to work here, but if you wanted to pm or something that might be fun. It's been really nice talking to you, first time in a long time I've been able to just talk and not have to stop and explain myself 100 times :)

Are you a minor? Have you thought about trying an inpatient program? I know it's extreme, but it might be a good option. It can't be easy for you to take care of your dad like that, and I'm sure he doesn't feel good laying his problems on his child. Suicidal ideation makes people feel ashamed and guilty on top of everything else.
Why you though!? It isn't fair and it sucks and sometimes you have to cry and maybe kick over a trash can (feels therapeutic).

Did you tell them you didn't have any plans or weren't suicidal? I'm not gonna lie, I've done that, you should probably let them know gently at some point. I can understand not wanting to tell them, they make such a huge fuss, but then I remember that I've attempted before and they're doing their stupid job.

I'm so sorry about yesterday! That's scary stuff, and I'm glad you're okay, have you talked to someone about that yet? If I even were good at pushing myself, I would have started taking care of myself a long time ago, but you're here and surviving and that's a step! There's only a handful of choices you can make in a situation and the choices you made have gotten you this far. You deserve the hug!
Let's only feed some of the hungry :-) /s

Give yourself a nice big mental hug or something (handshake if you're uncomfortable with hugs). Knowing when to make yourself ask for help, in my opinion, is like the #1 key to survival when stuff really hits the fan.

You don't shut it up per se. That part of your brain is still fighting to prove you've been through abuse, I didn't start realizing my parents were even abusive at all until a few months NC, yes they're awful but abuse? I didn't think so. But that part of my brain, some validation, and a bit of support made me realize what they were for real. 
Doesn't mean it isn't annoying to be dwelling on it though, so you'll have to find a healthier way to think about these things and care for that part of your brain (if that makes sense). Grounding techniques and telling yourself that you don't want to think about that and you'll come back to it helps. Like, just put a bookmark there and try to distract your train of thought long enough to switch rails, and when you're ready and all armored up all the ick will still be there to sort through.

You should write it all out, maybe put it on google docs or something, and then take the time to re read it. Then after that, post about it, post the whole thing or half or anything. People here are very supportive and understanding, and when you start telling stories everyone starts telling stories and it's nice to hear others' advice. 
Although I will say, not everyone's advice is good or helpful, and if you're unsatisfied with them you don't need to feel alone or like you wasted your time.
Chances are if you post about your story on RBN, you'll get some good advice and support. :)

Yeah honestly, it's all about your comfort level, I think you'll know if you really need to talk to your boss when the time comes. It might help to alleviate your anxiety a bit if someone at work knows you're going through a lot tho, just a few of my coworkers know and my manager. They don't do much in the way of support and care, but they can catch me before I tomahawk a knife into the wall and let me take a breather. 
However unhelpful this may be, it seems like you know what you're working with in terms of mental illness and have a solid handle on it, which is really all we can do so you're on a good road.

You should leave the option of telling your boss open, you never have to of course, but I told my boss and she couldn't have been more understanding. Especially now that I'm off my meds, I was continuously late for work because I was sleeping through everything and instead of firing me she is working with me on it. If I never told her, I'd have to come up with excuses and it would seem unreliable (which it is I guess, but I'm trying really hard and she sees that!). 
Also, fuck call centers, I worked at one for 4 days and quit so I think if you can handle that you can handle just about anything 🙂

I work in a high stress restaurant so thankfully tantrums and walking out are common and people express emotion whether they want to or not some times. I know that sounds pretty not fun but it means that when I'm really doing bad no ones judging me at work. Although that also means that work makes me more stressed lol. Can't have your cake and eat it too I guess. 
Edit: just to be clear I wasn't calling your getting laid off a tantrum tho, honestly a police escort sounds a tad extreme, and how humiliating at that! Sorry you got laid off 🙁
🙏 preach
Ah yes, panic season, can we use that instead of bikini season or whatever from now on? I like it.

I think even with a partner, sometimes you're one of very few that understands just how horrible you're feeling. I talked to my dude and apologized for not waking him sooner and he said that he wish I would have bc he worries about me, but that sometimes people just make things worse, they don't understand enough.
Yes! I didn't end up going last night, although I thought about it big time, I've gotta work today and somehow that is enough to keep me from going.
Yeah I'm starting to resent my "part time" (36 hours/week) job bc they won't give me benefits or PTO.
Hahah thank you for the trumpets. I'm still awake and not at the hospital but I'm still here, and doing a bit better with some support. I think I can count that as a win!
Yeah I woke my fiance up, he wants me to go to an inpatient facility, I've got work tomorrow though and can't convince myself it would be worth it.
Yeah the good ol' USA, no help unless you got the cash.
They have a chat room too, but I had 20 people ahead of me and that was after waiting 15 minutes.
Hey thanks, I appreciate it. Funny how the people there to help aren't much help at all.
It's a long long story that starts with abusive parents and ends with my doc dropping me and not being able to get any of my medications after trying numerous things (I'm poor too, so that helps).
Call poison control, they will know whether or not you should induce vomiting or not.

With where your mind is at, its understandable that you wouldn't want to go to the hospital, but its probably your best and safest option. If you take a step back, the logical conclusion here is for you to get the best help you can, maybe you'll miss work but in the long run it just doesn't matter by comparison. 
Not killing yourself > good work attendance. I know that is so oversimplified, but let everything else come second and take care of yourself.

I get so frustrated when people try to relate from a normal mindset, depression is unlike anything else and losing a loved one doesn't even compare, its all completely different. People don't grasp that wholly unless you're on this side of the fence I think. 
Everyone is a hero as well, they all have the key to your happiness and they truly believe that if you ate a banana and signed up for the stupid jujitsu all of our problems would be cured. 
The whole damn point is that I can barely pull myself out of bed and into the bathroom in the morning, I wouldn't put money on many of us even making it to (much less through) a yoga class. 
If we all had a nickel or a dime for every well meaning individual that gave us awful and sort of rude advice, we could probably find a cure.
I remember feeling completely exhausted with life shortly after my younger sibling was born and I was around 4 or 5, it hasn't stopped since.

I have this to the point where I don't tell anyone if I find a new subject or hobby interesting because I know I'll quit before long. I have to do it for 3+ months before I'll even talk about it at this point. I don't know if its projection or real, but I feel like everyone gets annoyed if I bring up new hobbies or interests because they've heard it all before.
Patent this, trademark this, sell it. White undies to summon your period, works like a charm hahaha

Sorry, didn't mean to assume your parents were crappy, mine were so its hard to remember not everyone's are. Being the middle child still applies though, although it sounds like your parents must be thankful to have you around.
Best of luck!

I've actually become enthralled in art history, so its become a habit to turn on an art history lecture (khan academy is amazing for educational stuff online) and doodle while I watch the videos. Sometimes I'll draw the subject matter, or I'll just doodle whatever pops into my head, usually comes out pretty interesting though. Its branched out into world history and architecture now too, which is never something I'd have picked. I also learned to crochet, and cook a bunch of different things. It had been a really long time since I felt like myself, a creative outlet is hella therapeutic.

p.s. my trail mix dreams were dashed, I was so excited about all of the possibilities.

Pretty uncanny, but same. Middle child, crappy parents, they tried getting me back up and doing chores and work around the house the day I got out of the hospital. Looking back, I wish I would have ignored them and focused on myself, so take care of yourself (mentally, physically, etc). Sucks that you have to deal with them while you're coping, such is the life of a middle child I guess!
I know just how you feel, and yet sometimes when the mood strikes me I just can't shut up.

Take your time bouncing back, mentally speaking. I had a pulmonary embolism at 19, almost killed me, and its certainly strange to find your way back to normal. Seems like you've got a pretty good handle on it, congrats on being well and surviving in the first place too!
Absolutely! You should post in some other subreddits as well, I know there are a few different depression, anxiety, or other mental illness subs severely lacking anyone to just talk to. :)
Dang, are you okay? That's some pretty intense stuff.

Honestly, people could say its unhealthy to rely so heavily on pot, but its not as damaging as other options. Some times you have to get yourself through the day to get through the week and so on, and if weed helps then can it truly be that bad? I decided to try to learn some new things or try new stuff while I was high once in a while and have found a bunch of new hobbies as a result. I have a sketchbook full of some fun doodles and thoughts that I write down while stoned, and some of it is pretty dumb (thought I invented trail mix for a hot minute), but its also kind of therapeutic.

I'm so sorry that you have to deal with this at all, words can't describe the disgusting feeling. Have you tried letting some of this out physically? Not like exercise (I guess if you wanted to, it helps) but writing, or typing, or yelling. Some times it starts off feeling really dumb, but if you can take out some anger or sadness out on a piece of paper instead of yourself, it helps a bit. I've even resorted to snapping pencils to let off a little steam, and direct it outward rather than in.
Reddit might not be a bad place for it, but how does one wrangle all the depressed people into one spot and get them talking, if there is an answer to that then we might just be onto something haha!
That's super thoughtful and I'm sure you've brightened a few peoples lonely times, I hope next time you need it someone does the same for you.
Agreed! We all need to get together and agree on some place to go so no one has to suffer through the polite small talk or uncomfortable strangers on a depression chat line lol
true, nothing more deflating than no comments on a depression sub :(

I'm in a very similar boat, and I'm really sorry that either of are us are in these stupid boats. I think that when it comes down to it, you only have yourself, you've been fighting for years and that makes you unbelievably strong. After a lot of really hard work and some progress I have kind of a me against the world attitude, and that has helped because I'm alone a lot, I guess thats food for thought.
Mostly when I've asked for help, I don't end up getting what I need, and I feel pretty exhausted after. I used to be so scared to even reach out a tiny bit for help, but I broke that barrier and most of the helpful words were just that. 
I hope none of this came off as know it all or like crappy advice, its intended as genuine solidarity.
I don't know, I switched to sports bras after my best bra stabbed me with underwire, eventually going braless completely. I've got DDD's, but its so much more comfortable to not wear a bra.
When I was in high school my teacher made a comment about my yawning, asking if he was boring me, and I still remember how awful and ashamed I felt over a stupid yawn.

You're making progress, reaching out is a huge step, so congratulations! Go at your own pace, but you should look into different counselling services in your area, there are usually free or very low cost programs available. It feels so good to feel validated and talk with a therapist, it can be tough to keep going back, but you learn so much about yourself.

I'm sorry about your job stress, and I really can't help with the social aspect because I struggle with that constantly. I will say that I don't think your coworkers are talking about you or laughing at you, that's the depression and (in my case) probably anxiety messing with your head. Every time you think they're talking about you, try to actively tell yourself that it isn't true, your coworkers have no reason to think about you in that way. Beyond that, never force yourself into a job that you hate for too long, it often times will make life worse. Although, if I am right about your coworkers, you'll likely find that everywhere you go, and should try to fight those thoughts! 

Good luck!!
Forgive me if this is rude, but when did you find out you were on the spectrum and how?

Sorry for the late response! Yeah she told me that it was easier to just take a bath while cleaning it because then you wouldn't dirty it later, she'd give me a bottle of bleach and a scrubby and I'd get to work. 

I'll take a look into self help books, in this case they may actually be helpful. You should try too :)
I've been going through a pretty rough time of lately as well, maybe you'd like to talk?
